brief.headline: Credit report access complaints climb, with Equifax over-represented on identity-verification lockouts
brief.what_is_happening: Monthly complaints about being unable to get a credit report or score rose to 1,919 in July and 1,930 in August 2026, after a dip to 1,281 in June. The recent three-month average of 1,710 compares with a 1,491.33 baseline average, a velocity of 1.1461 (rank 9 of 79). In the AI-reviewed sample, consumers allege they were blocked from accounts after submitting identity documents, locked out because of outdated contact details, or unable to reach a live person. Others allege missing or suppressed file information and uninvestigated disputes. These are unverified claims.
brief.who_is_affected: Consumers trying to access or freeze their credit reports and scores at the national credit bureaus, particularly those with outdated phone or email contact details or who fail identity verification. Some allege harm to employment and housing prospects and continued charges for subscription services they cannot use. Complaints are concentrated in FL (16.3%), TX (14.5%) and CA (8.4%).
brief.likely_root_cause: Hypothesis to test: identity-verification and account-recovery flows reject or stall legitimate consumers, for example on document uploads, contact-detail mismatches, or lost phone numbers. Automated support with no clear path to a human may leave them stuck. A possible contributor is a recent change in authentication or fraud-prevention settings, though the evidence does not confirm this. The sample is small, so the mix of causes is uncertain.
brief.process_or_control_to_check: Review consumer identity verification and account-recovery workflows, including document-upload review, handling of outdated contact information, escalation from automated support to live agents, credit freeze management access, and subscription cancellation paths. Also check dispute intake and reinvestigation handling for file-not-found or suppressed-file cases.
brief.regulatory_area: Consumer credit reporting: access to consumer file disclosures, dispute investigation and accuracy, and identity verification and customer support practices.
evidence: Monthly complaints reached 1,919 in 2026-07 and 1,930 in 2026-08, versus 1,281 in 2026-06.
Recent monthly average of 1,710 versus baseline monthly average of 1,491.33 (velocity 1.1461, rank 9 of 79).
EQUIFAX, INC. has a lift of 2.011 on 3,090 complaints, while Experian is 0.843 on 1,325 and TransUnion is 0.271 on 508, so over-representation is not uniform across the large bureaus.
Smaller names show elevated lift on very low counts: Credit Karma 83.424 (14 complaints), ID Analytics 4.438 (9), FNIS 2.886 (15), LexisNexis 2.346 (59).
32.4% of the 39-narrative AI sample cite being blocked after submitting identity documents.
29.4% of the AI sample cite lockouts tied to outdated contact info or no human support.
23.5% of the sample cite disputes not investigated or inaccurate data uncorrected, and 14.7% cite missing or disappeared credit file information.
Only 3 narratives were available in recent months, with a templated share of 0.0%, and the AI sample size was 39 with mean severity 3.18 out of 5.

checks.name: size
checks.reason: The brief ties the signal to Equifax, whose lift is 2.011 on 3,090 complaints versus Experian 0.843 and TransUnion 0.271, so the over-representation is not just company size.

checks.name: templating
checks.reason: The templated share of recent narratives is 0.0%, well under the 30% threshold.

checks.name: concentration
checks.reason: The top states are FL 16.3%, TX 14.5% and CA 8.4%, and 3,090 Equifax, 1,325 Experian and 508 TransUnion complaints spread the signal across several states and companies.

checks.name: thin_evidence
checks.reason: Only 3 narratives exist in the recent months, below the minimum of 10, even though the AI sample of 39 is adequate and the identity-verification and lockout themes cover about 62% of it.

checks.name: seasonality
checks.reason: Counts rose from 1,281 in June to 1,919 in July and 1,930 in August, so the recent average of 1,710 does not rest on one peak month and the latest month is the high point.

skeptic.note: Rejected because only 3 narratives exist in the recent months, too few to support the identity-verification root cause, even though the other four checks pass.
